alt.en: A printed page of English prose headed "cclx" and "Table Hymns.": "(a) The hymn Rock from whose store we have eaten is of unknown authorship. It is based on the paragraphs of the Grace after Meals", ending "from a rendering by Mr I. Zangwill)."
alt.es: Una página impresa de prosa en inglés con los encabezados "cclx" y "Table Hymns.": "(a) The hymn Rock from whose store we have eaten is of unknown authorship. It is based on the paragraphs of the Grace after Meals", que termina "from a rendering by Mr I. Zangwill)."

caption.en: Israel Abrahams's note in the 1914 annotated Singer's prayer book: the hymn is of unknown authorship, built on the grace after meals, and, as Baer pointed out, never mentions the Sabbath.
caption.es: La nota de Israel Abrahams en la edición anotada de 1914 del libro de oraciones de Singer: el himno es de autor desconocido, está construido sobre la bendición después de las comidas y, como señaló Baer, nunca menciona el sabbat.

source: Israel Abrahams, Annotated Edition of the Authorised Daily Prayer Book (London: Eyre and Spottiswoode, 1914), Appendix IV, "Table Hymns", p. cclx, note (a)
library: University of Toronto, Pratt Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive annotatededition00unknuoft (library call number AIC-2315), p. cclx (image n279)

alt.en: A short printed paragraph from one column of an encyclopedia: "When the whole collection of zemirot is used, they are not chanted to definite melodies ... the most frequent air is a German melody employed either with the "Yom Zeh le-Yisrael" of Isaac Luria or with the anonymous "Zur mi-Shello Akalnu.""
alt.es: Un breve párrafo impreso de una columna de enciclopedia: "When the whole collection of zemirot is used, they are not chanted to definite melodies ... the most frequent air is a German melody employed either with the "Yom Zeh le-Yisrael" of Isaac Luria or with the anonymous "Zur mi-Shello Akalnu.""

caption.en: The Jewish Encyclopedia's article on the zemirot, 1906: where only some of the table songs are sung, the most frequent air is a German melody, used with Yom Zeh le-Yisrael or with Tzur Mishelo.
caption.es: El artículo de la Jewish Encyclopedia sobre los zemirot, 1906: donde solo se cantan algunas de las canciones de mesa, la melodía más frecuente es una melodía alemana, que se usa con Yom Zeh le-Yisrael o con Tzur Mishelo.

source: Joseph Jacobs and Francis L. Cohen, "Zemirot", The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 12 (New York: Funk and Wagnalls, 1906), p. 659, right column
library: Cornell University Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)

alt.en: A printed page of Hebrew with vowel points, headed "Table Hymns." and "cclxi": seven lines of verse, the first two and the last two the same refrain, beginning "צור משלו אכלנו".
alt.es: Una página impresa en hebreo con signos vocálicos, con los encabezados "Table Hymns." y "cclxi": siete líneas de verso; las dos primeras y las dos últimas son el mismo estribillo, que empieza "צור משלו אכלנו".

caption.en: Tzur Mishelo's refrain and first verse in Hebrew, with the refrain again after it, as printed among the table hymns of the 1914 annotated Singer's prayer book.
caption.es: El estribillo y la primera estrofa de Tzur Mishelo en hebreo, con el estribillo de nuevo después, tal como se imprimieron entre los himnos de mesa de la edición anotada de 1914 del libro de oraciones de Singer.

source: Israel Abrahams, Annotated Edition of the Authorised Daily Prayer Book (London: Eyre and Spottiswoode, 1914), Appendix IV, "Table Hymns", p. cclxi, top (refrain, verse 1, refrain)

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Zemirot", "THE JEWISH ENCYCLOPEDIA" and "658", with the title "SABBATH REST" and the marking "Lento.": three lines of melody in 6/8, each with three verses of English under it, ending "A light and a joy to us is Sab-bath rest."
alt.es: Una página impresa de música con los encabezados "Zemirot", "THE JEWISH ENCYCLOPEDIA" y "658", el título "SABBATH REST" y la indicación "Lento.": tres líneas de melodía en 6/8, cada una con tres estrofas en inglés debajo, que terminan "A light and a joy to us is Sab-bath rest."

caption.en: The German melody as the Jewish Encyclopedia printed it in 1906 under the title "Sabbath Rest", the page our arrangement is read from; the English verses under it belong to Yom Zeh le-Yisrael, not to Tzur Mishelo.
caption.es: La melodía alemana tal como la imprimió la Jewish Encyclopedia en 1906 con el título "Sabbath Rest", la página de la que sale nuestro arreglo; las estrofas en inglés que lleva debajo son de Yom Zeh le-Yisrael, no de Tzur Mishelo.

source: Joseph Jacobs and Francis L. Cohen, "Zemirot", The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 12 (New York: Funk and Wagnalls, 1906), p. 658, "Sabbath Rest"
